name: Cell — The Unit of Life
desc: Complete classification of the Cell chapter: every box shows what it means, and its position in the tree is shown by the index badge.

children.name: Cell Theory
children.desc: The 3 basic rules that define what a cell is

children.name: Schleiden & Schwann
children.desc: 1838: all organisms are made of cells; cell is the basic unit

children.name: Virchow
children.desc: 1855: omnis cellula e cellula — cells arise from existing cells

children.name: Cell Types
children.desc: Two fundamental architectures of life

children.name: Prokaryotic
children.desc: No true nucleus — DNA floats free in cytoplasm

children.name: Bacteria
children.desc: 70S ribosomes, no membrane-bound organelles

children.name: Archaea
children.desc: Like bacteria but distinct biochemistry

children.name: Eukaryotic
children.desc: True nucleus + membrane-bound organelles

children.name: Plant cell
children.desc: Has cell wall, chloroplasts and large vacuole

children.name: Cell wall
children.desc: Cellulose; gives shape and support

children.name: Chloroplasts
children.desc: Site of photosynthesis — makes food

children.name: Animal cell
children.desc: No cell wall; centrioles and lysosomes present

children.name: Membrane Systems
children.desc: The factory floor — membranes divide the cell into work stations

children.name: Plasma membrane
children.desc: Outer boundary — the gatekeeper of the cell

children.name: Fluid mosaic model
children.desc: Phospholipid bilayer with floating proteins

children.name: Selective permeability
children.desc: Lets some molecules pass, blocks others

children.name: Endomembrane system
children.desc: ER, Golgi and lysosomes work as one transport chain

children.name: Endoplasmic reticulum
children.desc: Membrane factory that makes and moves molecules

children.name: Rough ER
children.desc: Has ribosomes — makes proteins

children.name: Smooth ER
children.desc: Makes lipids and detoxifies

children.name: Golgi apparatus
children.desc: Packs and ships proteins like a post office

children.name: Lysosomes
children.desc: Suicidal bags — digest waste and invaders

children.name: Vacuoles
children.desc: Storage tanks for water, salts and waste

children.name: Genetic Material
children.desc: Where the blueprint of life is stored and read

children.name: Nucleus
children.desc: Brain of the cell — controls all activities

children.name: Nuclear envelope
children.desc: Double membrane with pores for traffic

children.name: Nucleolus
children.desc: Makes ribosome subunits

children.name: Chromatin
children.desc: DNA + histones — condenses into chromosomes

children.name: Ribosomes
children.desc: Protein factories — read mRNA, build proteins

children.name: 70S ribosome
children.desc: Prokaryotic type: 50S + 30S

children.name: 80S ribosome
children.desc: Eukaryotic type: 60S + 40S

children.name: Energy Centres
children.desc: Powerhouses that supply ATP for every activity

children.name: Mitochondria
children.desc: Powerhouse of the cell — makes ATP by respiration

children.name: Cristae
children.desc: Folded inner membrane — more surface for reactions

children.name: Matrix
children.desc: Inner fluid holding the Krebs cycle enzymes

children.name: Chloroplasts
children.desc: Kitchen of the cell — traps sunlight to make food

children.name: Thylakoids
children.desc: Discs stacked as grana — catch light energy

children.name: Stroma
children.desc: Fluid where the Calvin cycle builds glucose

children.name: Cell Division
children.desc: How cells copy themselves to grow and reproduce

children.name: Mitosis
children.desc: One division — identical copies; growth and repair

children.name: Prophase
children.desc: Chromosomes condense, spindle forms

children.name: Metaphase
children.desc: Chromosomes line up at the equator

children.name: Anaphase
children.desc: Sister chromatids are pulled apart

children.name: Telophase
children.desc: Two new nuclei form, cell splits

children.name: Meiosis
children.desc: Two divisions — halves chromosome number; makes gametes

children.name: Meiosis I
children.desc: Homologous chromosomes separate

children.name: Meiosis II
children.desc: Sister chromatids separate — 4 haploid cells

legend: Index badge (1.2) = position of the box counted from the top of the classification
Grey line under a name = the meaning of that box (desc)
Tap any box → its unit/topic position and full meaning
